$comment: Every distribution in this repository that declares a version nobody can
install, with the reason that state is acceptable. Measured by
`scripts/declared_publication_sweep.py`, guarded by
`tests/architecture/test_declared_publication.py`.
## Why this file exists at all
`test_module_version_sync.py` proves a module's three version surfaces
AGREE. It cannot prove the agreed version EXISTS. `dotmac-integration`
reads 0.1.0a2 on all three surfaces and the version-identity guard passes,
while the newest tag is dotmac-integration-v0.1.0a1 — internal consistency
and publication are different questions, and only the first one had a
guard. A consumer reading the repository, the changelog or
docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md and pinning ==0.1.0a2 gets a resolver error.
## What a row here does and does not mean
A row means the state is KNOWN and someone has said why. It is not
permission to leave it there, and it is emphatically not a reason to edit
the declared version down to match the index: that would make the
repository agree with the registry by discarding the work the number
describes, and the changelog entry for the unpublished version would then
belong to nothing.
The repair is not always a release, either. `dotmac-imports` was reported
as an anomaly BECAUSE it was release-allowlisted with no tag; the ruling
was that the allowlist row was the wrong half, and it was removed rather
than the module published. Two states this file must keep distinct:
* INTENDED — the distribution is meant to be unpublished right now.
The row records the decision so
the next reader does not undo it by dispatching a release.
* OUTSTANDING — a version is genuinely owed to consumers. The row
records evidence a decision still needs. Two worked examples have now
passed through and been removed on release: `dotmac-integration`
0.1.0a2 (released as a3) and `dotmac-kernel` 0.1.0a67. A row that
expires on its own release is the healthiest shape an entry here has.
Both are recorded the same way and neither is a pass. The reason text is
where the difference lives, which is why the guard requires a premise
rather than a label.
## Two directions, both failures
A distribution entering this state without a row fails — that is a version
silently promised to consumers. A row whose distribution has since been
published ALSO fails and must be removed in the same change as the release,
because a ledger that only grows stops describing anything (ADR-0018).
## The oracle is a git tag
The release workflows write a tag only after `verify-registry` has
installed the exact published version from the private index and registered
its manifest, so a tag is this repository's own assertion that a version is
installable — stronger than 'an upload succeeded'. The index is not queried
directly: that needs an authenticated URL, which makes the check
un-runnable at PR time and offline, and a gate that cannot run is not a
gate. The stated cost is that a publication whose tag step failed reads
here as unpublished — which is exactly the state
`recover-module-release.yml` exists to repair, so reporting it is correct.

dotmac-deployment-foundation.reason: DECLARED, NEVER BUILT. 0.4.0a1 is the successor allocated 2026-09-04. It is a MINOR bump rather than a seventh alpha of the 0.3.0 line because it names a widening of a closed authorization vocabulary: `recover` re-enters authorization.OPERATIONS against an executor for the act it names -- authorized recovery of a FAILED PRODUCTION SYSTEM, with its own RecoveryExecutionPlanV1, an ExecutionGrant, the replay coordinate, Control settlement, a signed result, and the three bindings a rehearsal does not take. A consumer reading OPERATIONS gets a third member it did not have. It has NOT been built and must not be until the Lane 3 exposure rehearsal passes on the exact SHA under release; that lane today produces no receipt at all, so no foundation candidate is publishable. ITS PREDECESSOR WAS NEVER BUILT EITHER, AND THAT IS A FIRST FOR THIS FACILITY: 0.3.0a6 was declared 2026-09-03 and retired unbuilt on 2026-09-04. There is no wheel, no CandidateArtifact.v1 receipt and therefore NO CandidateDisposition.v1 -- the log dispositions built artifacts, anchored by receipt_path and receipt_digest and hash-chained from the receipt's own digest, and there is nothing to anchor to. Symmetry there would be wrong rather than merely unnecessary, provably: adding 0.3.0a6 to SUPERSEDED in tests/architecture/test_version_binding_guard.py fails test_a_superseded_candidate_is_still_refused_for_a_second_build, because the guard reads records and finds none for a version never built. EXPECTED_ENTRIES stays 4. 0.3.0a6 IS NONETHELESS A SPENT NAME, spent by DOCUMENTS rather than by bytes: while it was the declared identity, main advertised it in the package CHANGELOG, in docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md, in the poetry.lock path-package line, in this file, and inside the rendered deploy/rendered/docker-compose.yml labels via io.dotmac.deployment.configuration.digest. Re-declaring it would recreate 0.3.0a2's two-contracts defect with the documents instead of the bytes. NO MACHINE ORACLE REFUSES 0.3.0a6: the version-binding guard reads tags, candidate receipts and dispositions, and this name is in none of them. ABANDONED_UNBUILT in the binding-guard test states the freshness expectation longhand; it is an expectation, not an enforcement, and the population is recorded as unmonitored rather than covered. THE EARLIER BYTES ARE UNCHANGED BY ANY OF THIS: 0.3.0a5 was built exactly once on 2026-09-03 from 27bee8fc43919a5ed7f4853ccdedc2f996ad8d86 (run 33780438726, candidate artifact 9903418260, wheel sha256 17b3464ede04a182958753b493d08c5f06e2b5643960c113ecf6584d4ed56e1b, sdist sha256 df9753e0ab6dddbfbbbaa6f468d3d633fa66088fb3b89d0d9f4cc7c7d969ab18, expires 2026-12-02T16:44:35Z), its CandidateArtifact.v1 receipt is docs/inventories/foundation-candidate-0.3.0a5.json, and it is recorded SUPERSEDED and publishable=false at CandidateDisposition.v1 sequence 4; it is NOT defective, merely overtaken. 0.3.0a4 is preserved and separately superseded/unpublishable (sequence 3); 0.3.0a3 remains Platform CP's bootstrap input, resolved by run and artifact id rather than by the index, and is likewise superseded for release; 0.3.0a2 is invalidated. None of them may ever be rebuilt or relabelled. Remove this row only when 0.4.0a1 is published by an authorized release.
